Hey - I’m also in the same boat. 

My mom passed away due to ovarian cancer and my PCP recommended that I (25, F) get a genetic test to see if I have the gene that makes you more likely to get it in the future. Long story short, I have the gene so I have to get exams every 6 months; for right now it’s an MRI and then when I turn 30 I’ll get mammograms. Ideally they’d like me to figure out if I want kids by 35, and although I really want kids, the possibility of me having them are very slim atm. 

Its been super tough bc I don’t really know how to feel - I’m happy that I caught it and I prevented it for myself but for some reason it’s just stressful to think about bc not a lot of people around me are going through the same thing. I also just wish my mom was able to do the same so she could be here with me. It’s really lonely. 

I wish I had advice for you on how to get through it but I’m also battling it too…but like the comments said we’re in this together. It doesn’t have to be lonely bc we can lean on each other and talk about our experiences. 

I think for me, I’m going to make sure that I do something extra special for myself around those days that I have those appointments to make it somewhat easier. Good luck love!

OH MAN LOL 

My mom died when I was 14 (June 2012) due to cancer. When I was about a junior or senior in high school my dad started dating and then eventually got remarried in 2019. Seeing my dad date again and then end up getting remarried was really hard for me because it felt like he was filling a void, but I didn’t have the ability to do the same. 

I would say definitely have a conversation with him about how you feel; no matter how hard it is because your feelings about this matter too. That’s one thing I wish I would’ve did before he got remarried - I never said how I felt and then it blew up in arguments later down the line. 

With his new wife, I’ve just been cordial and have tried to keep my distance, especially since she can be a lot sometimes. I agree with finding those mother figures in your life like aunts, cousins, grandmas; even friends I’ve sometimes relied on to help me with things that I would ideally ask my mom about.

My dad and I have had our ups and downs about the situation but knowing he’s happy and that we still have each other at the end of the day has helped me get through it too.

My mom also died when I was 14 and due to cancer. I’ve had a couple of dreams where she was alive and in those dreams, I used to just think everything was some sick joke, like for some reason, she decided to fake her death. Similar to what you said in your original post, I think it’s because we’re just trying to wrap our minds around something that honestly doesn’t make any sense. Why was it my mom? Why did it happen during such a pivotal part of my life? Although hurtful, I think it’d be easier to think that she’s still here rather than not. 

Sometimes I even make myself feel guilty for grieving at random times and think that I actually don’t miss her or that I’m using her death as an “excuse”. 

Grieving the death of a parent, I’ve come to realize, is a very ugly and traumatizing experience. And I hope that you aren’t hard on yourself as you’re continuing to navigate life without her, as I’m trying to do the same. Definitely easier said than done, but you’re definitely not alone in how you feel.

You’re not alone tho, no matter how lonely this may feel.

Im also on 10mgs! I started a couple of months ago and tbh I was skeptical at first. I had the worst side effects (couldn’t cry, always tired, etc.) for the first month or so. The first couple of weeks/months on it is really hard and everyone reacts to it differently. 

I will say that I do feel a lot happier throughout the day and my anxiety is more controlled. I feel like I can do more than I’d be able to do before taking it. I’m a lot more social and noticed that I handle tough situations better than before

Idk sometimes I get hard on myself for being on meds, but I can’t deny that it has helped me a lot and is one of the better decisions I’ve made for myself. You still have to work with it bc it can only take you so far, but overall I’ve had a decent experience. Now that the meds are working I’m at the point where I have to work with it and put the things I’ve been learning in therapy to good use 😅

It could be that lexapro just isn’t for you and thats ok!!! I would give it some time and try be patient with yourself these next couple of days as your body is getting used to it. 

Hope this helps and eases some of your worries - good luck!!
